cim_eredeti: Adobe Firefly Price 2026: Is It Free, What Plans Cost
szoveg_eredeti:
Adobe Firefly’s standalone subscription runs from $9.99 a month (Standard, 2,000 generative credits) to $199.99 a month (Premium, 50,000 credits), as of September 2026. A free tier exists too, but it covers only a curated set of models with a daily allowance Adobe does not publish. This guide answers the questions people ask most — what Firefly is, whether the free tier is usable, what the paid plans cost, whether it does animation, and how it differs from Figma — with prices from Adobe’s own pages, then compares it honestly against Krea and the wider field.

All Firefly numbers come from Adobe’s Firefly plans page as of September 2026; Krea numbers from krea.ai/pricing. Prices change — check the live pages before deciding.

Every price, credit count, and limit here was verified against the vendor’s published pages in September 2026: Adobe’s Firefly overview, the plans page, the generative credits FAQ, the Firefly video page, and Figma’s AI page. Where Adobe does not publish an exact number — the free tier’s daily generation count, for example — we say so rather than guess. The example images are raw, single Krea 2 generations from the exact prompts beside them; none were made with Firefly, and the captions say so.

Adobe Firefly is Adobe’s generative AI product family: a web app (plus iOS and Android apps) that generates images, vector graphics, video clips, audio, animations, and talking avatars — and the same models embedded inside Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, Lightroom, and Adobe Express. Photoshop’s Generative Fill is Firefly.

Two things distinguish it from most generators. First, the Firefly web app is now a multi-model hub: alongside Adobe’s own models you can run partner models — Google’s Gemini 3 image model, OpenAI’s GPT Image, Kling, Runway, Luma AI, ElevenLabs — as Adobe’s overview page puts it, “Access models from Adobe, Google, OpenAI, Runway, and more, with one login.”

Second, Adobe positions its first-party models as “commercially safe”: trained, per Adobe, “on licensed content from Adobe Stock and public domain content where copyright has expired,” with Content Credentials attached to outputs. For legal teams at large companies this is Firefly’s strongest argument — no other mainstream generator makes an equivalent training-data claim. It applies to Adobe’s own models, not to the partner models inside the same app.

Where it stops: Firefly is a generation feature-set attached to the Adobe ecosystem, not a standalone creative pipeline. Its own image models have historically trailed the frontier on photorealism and prompt adherence — which is why Adobe now resells Gemini, GPT Image, and Kling inside the app — and running those partner models is what burns your credits.

Yes, with real limits. Firefly’s free tier gives daily generations across image, video, and audio on a curated set of models, and the allowance refreshes every day. Adobe does not publish the exact daily count on its plans page, and states that generations, features, and models can change. Premium models and higher volumes need a paid plan and its monthly generative credits.

A useful yardstick from Adobe’s own video page: the $9.99 Standard plan’s 2,000 credits buy up to about 40 five-second videos a month.

Firefly free-tier recipe (no image here — we don’t fake Firefly outputs):

Go to firefly.adobe.com and sign in with a free Adobe account. Pick Text to Image, set the model to an Adobe Firefly model, aspect ratio 16:9, and paste: “Product photo of a ceramic espresso cup on stone, soft morning side light, editorial style.” Generate; the daily allowance refreshes tomorrow.

Variation tips: stay on Adobe’s own models to stretch the free daily allowance; use Generative Fill inside the Firefly web editor for touch-ups instead of regenerating the whole frame.

Yes. Firefly generates video from text or from an image (photo, illustration, 2D or 3D render), through the Firefly Video Model and partner video models: Google Veo 3.1, Luma AI Ray3, Kling 3.0, and Runway Gen-4.5. Per Adobe’s video generator page, most models generate clips up to 8 seconds (some up to 15), downloadable as MP4 up to 4K, in 16:9 or 9:16. The web app also makes animated avatars and audio (voiceover, sound effects).

The practical limits: clips are short, video burns credits fast (about 50 credits per five-second Standard-plan video, by Adobe’s 40-videos-per-2,000-credits figure), and unlimited video generation sits on the $199.99 Premium tier. The free daily generations cover experiments; sustained video work needs Pro Plus or Premium — or a tool priced around video from the start. For the broader landscape, see the best free AI video generators in 2026.

In the Firefly web app choose Text to Video (or Image to Video and upload a still). Select the Firefly Video Model, 16:9, and prompt: “Slow dolly-in on a ceramic espresso cup on a stone counter, steam rising, morning light, shallow depth of field.” Keep motion verbs simple — one camera move per clip.

Variation tips: image-to-video with a still you already like gives far more control than text-to-video; describe the camera move, not the whole scene again.

No. The question comes up because both are “design tools” in casual speech, and Adobe famously tried (and failed, in 2023) to acquire Figma — but they occupy different categories. Figma is a collaborative interface-design platform: teams design and prototype software products in one shared place. Firefly is a generative engine: it makes images, video, and audio from prompts.

The overlap is narrowing from the other direction, though. Figma’s AI page now advertises image editing and generation inside Figma, plus Figma Weave — “AI workflows for imagery, video, audio, and more.” Choose by the surrounding workflow: Figma if the deliverable is a product interface, Firefly if it’s Adobe-centric visual content, or a dedicated generator like Krea if the generation itself is the work.

The clean way to frame it: Firefly is generation bolted into the Adobe ecosystem; Krea is a generation-first studio where the models, editor, upscaler, and video tools are the product.

Where Firefly genuinely wins. If your day already lives in Photoshop, Generative Fill inside your existing file beats any external tool. If your legal team requires licensed training data, Adobe’s first-party models are the mainstream answer. And a single Adobe login now fronts Google, OpenAI, Kling, and Runway models — convenient if you already pay for Creative Cloud.

Where Krea wins. Krea’s free tier serves its frontier in-house model: Krea 2 with style-reference control, 100 compute units every day, plus basic upscaling to 2K and limited LoRA training — no credit card. Paid plans start at $9/month for 5,000 compute units and unlock the full model library (the same third-party image and video models Firefly resells, and more), the AI image editor, the 8K-class Enhancer, video generation, and the commercial license. Krea is built for iteration speed — generate, restyle, edit, enhance — rather than as a feature inside a document editor.

Where Krea stops. The free tier is Krea 2 images only: no video models, no full model library, no 3D or lipsync, no Nodes, and no commercial license — those sit on paid plans (verified on krea.ai/pricing, September 2026). And Krea makes no licensed-training-data claim comparable to Adobe’s; if that is a hard requirement, Firefly’s first-party models are the safer pick.

lead: Az Adobe Firefly havi 10 és 200 dollár közötti csomagokat kínál, miközben már olyan külső modelleket is integrál, mint a Gemini 3 vagy a Kling.
osszefoglalo:
Az [Adobe Firefly](https://firefly.adobe.com) önálló előfizetései havi 9,99 dollártól egészen 199,99 dollárig terjednek a kreditek számától függően. Az eszköz legnagyobb újdonsága, hogy **már egyetlen felületen keresztül érhetők el a partnercégek modelljei** is, így az Adobe saját megoldásai mellett a Google [Gemini](https://gemini.google.com) 3, az [OpenAI](https://openai.com) GPT Image, a [Kling](https://klingai.com), a [Runway](https://runwayml.com) és a [Luma](https://lumalabs.ai) AI is használható.

A rendszerben a videógenerálás kiemelten sok kreditet fogyaszt, egy 5 másodperces klip körülbelül 50 kreditbe kerül. Az Adobe saját modelljei továbbra is **jogilag biztonságos, licencelt tartalmakkal kereskedelmi használatra optimalizáltak**, de ez a garancia a beépített külső partner modellekre már nem vonatkozik.

A konkurens [Krea](https://krea.ai) ezzel szemben havi 9 dollártól kínál fizetős csomagokat, és az ingyenes verziójában is napi 100 számítási egységet ad a saját [Krea](https://www.krea.ai) 2 modelljéhez. Míg az Adobe Firefly az alkotói munkafolyamatokba való beépülésével hódít, a [Krea](https://www.krea.ai/) a **gyors, generálás-központú iterációra fókuszál**.
miert_szamit: A magyar marketingeseknek és kreatívoknak a Firefly ideális választás, ha **közvetlenül a Photoshopban akarnak jogilag biztonságos képeket generálni**. Ha viszont a gyors kísérletezés és a költséghatékony képalkotás a cél, a Krea külső eszközként jobb alternatívát nyújt.
